papers.title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
papers.abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincar\'e duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.

papers.title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
papers.abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.

papers.title: Dimensions and maximal-dimensional components of higher commuting varieties of symmetric pairs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak p$ be the $(-1)$-eigenspace of a complex semisimple symmetric pair. For every $r\ge2$, we prove $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))\le \lfloor r\dim\mathfrak p/2\rfloor$ and show that every irreducible component is isotropic for a natural family of alternating forms. For a nonzero Hermitian pair with $\mathfrak g$ simple and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p^-\oplus\mathfrak p^+$, put $d=\dim\mathfrak p^+$ and $\ell=\operatorname{rk}(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k)$. Then \[ \dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=rd,\qquad \dim C_r(\mathfrak p)=\max\{rd,\,2d+(r-1)\ell\}. \] In this case we also determine the maximal-dimensional components of $C_r(\mathfrak p)$; for $r\ge3$, the only maximal-dimensional nilpotent components are $(\mathfrak p^+)^r$ and $(\mathfrak p^-)^r$. For arbitrary symmetric pairs, $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=ra+m$ for all large $r$, where $a$ is the largest dimension of an abelian subspace of $\mathfrak p$ consisting of nilpotent elements and $m$ is the dimension of the variety of such subspaces. Applications give dimension and component formulas for equivariant punctual Quot schemes under explicit framing conditions, and bounds for punctual Gorenstein loci refined by socle parity.

papers.title: Unipotent quotients in compactified Coxeter varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend Lusztig's description of quotients of Coxeter varieties by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups, to quotients of certain open neighbourhoods in the smooth compactification of Coxeter varieties. These quotients are products of an affine space with a Coxeter variety for an associated Levi quotient, and this result holds uniformly for any connected reductive group over a finite field. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Wang computing the invariants, under the action of unipotent subgroups, of the cohomology of the Deligne-Lusztig coverings of Coxeter varieties. We also prove that derived Alvis-Curtis duality sends the compactly supported cohomology of these coverings to their ordinary cohomology.

papers.title: Regularity of Totally Nonnegative Wonderful Compactification
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split real semisimple group of adjoint type. We prove that the cellular decomposition of the totally nonnegative part of its wonderful compactification is a regular CW complex, confirming a conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. In particular, the closure of every cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball. The proof combines a Bruhat atlas compatible with total positivity and a CL-labeling of the augmented face poset. The atlas models the strata locally with open Richardson varieties in the flag variety of a larger Kac-Moody group and identifies their totally nonnegative cells.

papers.title: Double Bruhat cells in symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: This paper studies the closures of the double Bruhat cells of symmetric spacess in its equivariant embeddings. We call them large double Bruhat varieties. Our aim is to establish the double Bruhat stratification as a natural setting for extending the geometry of Richardson varieties to symmetric spaces. For the wonderful compactification of the associated adjoint symmetric space, we show their scheme-theoretic intersections with the unique closed orbit are reduced unions of projected Richardson varieties. This connection with Richardson geometry on partial flag varieties supports large double Bruhat varieties as a natural class of subvarieties in symmetric-space embeddings. In positive characteristic, we prove that every equivariant embedding admits a Frobenius splitting compatible with all large double Bruhat varieties and all boundary divisors. These varieties are strongly F-regular, and globally F-regular when the ambient embedding is projective. In characteristic zero, they are of strongly F-regular type, and of globally F-regular type in the projective case; in particular, they are normal, Cohen-Macaulay, and have rational singularities.

papers.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|\pi_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $\pi$. We describe the restriction of $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ to the inertia subgroup in terms of Deligne-Lusztig theory. We prove this by computing the inertia action on the cohomology of shtuka spaces with depth-zero level structure. As an application, we prove that the Fargues--Scholze $L$-parameters agree with DeBacker--Reeder $L$-parameters over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$.

papers.title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$. We show that this inclusion is an isomorphism on the cuspidal part. In addition we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation $\pi$ of $G(F)$ defines a Hecke eigenvalue. As a byproduct we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation of $G(F)$ with an Iwahori fixed vector defines a ${\mathbb C}$-point on the Calogero-Moser space associated to $G$. We also show that for $G=PGL(N)$ the eigenvalues of certain "simplest non-trivial" Hecke operators are essentially equal to the values of the character of $\pi$ on regular elliptic elements. These results are parallel to some of the results of our previous publication where some analogous statements are proved in the case when $F$ is a finite field.

papers.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
papers.abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.

papers.title: Automorphisms of medium algebras and quasi-anisotropic real affine Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We study automorphisms of Hausel's medium algebras by identifying them with equivariant cohomology algebras of affine Schubert varieties of a complex reductive group $G$. The automorphisms in question are then given by the action of either complex automorphisms or real structures of $G$ on affine Schubert varieties. We focus on describing the fixed points of those automorphisms on the spectra of medium algebras, and prove that the torsion-free quotients of the corresponding coinvariant algebras are isomorphic to equivariant cohomology rings of fixed loci in affine Schubert varieties. In the case of real structures, this naturally leads to and involves the study of affine Grassmannians for quasi-anisotropic (also called quasi-compact) real reductive groups, closely related to recent work of O'Brien. We also discuss relations to automorphisms of Higgs bundle moduli and to symmetric pair variants of medium algebras.

papers.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
papers.abstract: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $\lambda$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $\lambda$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.

papers.title: Middle convolution for Lie algebra representations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a Lie algebra analogue of the middle convolution functor, which is defined on the category of modules over certain Lie algebras, including, as typical motivating examples, free Lie algebras, Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, and the holonomy Lie algebras of complements of hyperplane arrangements. First, we demonstrate that the middle convolution for Lie algebra representations can be regarded as a natural generalization of the infinitesimal analogue of the Long-Moody functor for Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras. Second, we show that our middle convolution recovers the Dettweiler-Reiter additive middle convolution for Fuchsian systems on the punctured Riemann sphere as a special case. Furthermore, we show that when applied to the holonomy Lie algebra of the complement of a hyperplane arrangement, our functor is compatible with Haraoka's middle convolution for logarithmic connections on such complements. Finally, we establish a Riemann-Hilbert correspondence between the middle convolution for the holonomy Lie algebra and the middle convolution for local systems on complements of hyperplane arrangements.

papers.title: Total positivity and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: We define a notion of total positivity for the symmetric space $G/K$ by taking the Hausdorff closure of the image of Lusztig's totally positive part $G_{>0}$ in $G/K$. We introduce double Bruhat cells for the symmetric space and define their totally positive pieces. We prove a cell decomposition of the totally nonnegative symmetric space, give explicit positive parametrizations of all cells, establish closure relations, and show that the transition maps between the two natural families of parametrizations are subtraction-free.

papers.title: Moduli of super-representations of quivers
papers.abstract: In this note, we construct moduli spaces of super-representations of quivers by extending King's Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT) framework to the super setting. Using the even part of super general linear groups and a parity-shifting operator, we construct moduli spaces that topologically parameterize super-representations of a fixed super-dimension. We also outline the construction of super quiver varieties for super-representations of framed quivers (without doubling); and realise super-Grassmannians and super-flag varieties as geometric quotients within this setting.

papers.title: Rotation fixed points of undecorated braid varieties and fusion rings of affine Lie algebras
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simply connected semisimple algebraic group. On the (undecorated) braid variety associated with a power of a Coxeter element, there is a finite-order autoequivalence, called the Zamolodchikov transformation, induced by cyclic rotation of words. In this paper, we show that the coarse moduli space of the fixed-point stack of this autoequivalence is isomorphic to the spectrum of the fusion ring of the corresponding affine Lie algebra. The above results also extend to twisted Coxeter elements, and the fusion rings of all affine Lie algebras are obtained in this way.

papers.title: Combinatorics of Mirkovi\'c-Vilonen cycles in twisted affine Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We investigate the explicit geometric and combinatorial structure of Mirkovi\'c-Vilonen (MV) cycles in twisted affine Grassmannians associated with special parahoric group schemes. Using the twist map on configuration spaces of decorated flags, we obtain an explicit parametrization of twisted MV cycles by Lusztig data. We show that the changes between reduced words are governed by the usual Lusztig transformations for the reductive group arising from ramified geometric Satake correspondence. As a consequence, the moment polytopes of twisted MV cycles coincide with the usual MV polytopes for this group. Our construction applies to all special parahoric subgroups in the tamely ramified setting.

papers.title: Ramified Quivers with Potentials, Monodromy Characters, and Cluster Bases I
papers.abstract: We construct categorical models and cluster characters for skew-symmetrizable cluster algebras admitting good ramified realizations. Goodness is equivalent to nondegenerate realizability. When a reddening sequence is given, it is enough to check sign coherence of the arrow types along that sequence. Triangular extensions with arbitrary connecting bimodule types preserve goodness when both component matrices admit reddening sequences. Consequently, every matrix obtained from one vertex by triangular extensions and mutations admits a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization for every compatible positive integral symmetrizer. For a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization, the monodromy $F$-polynomials satisfy mutation for all finite decorated representations, without a rigidity hypothesis. A full initial order determines valued universal presentations and their cluster characters. Under the reachability condition, these characters form a basis of the middle cluster algebra for arbitrary geometric coefficients, with frozen variables inverted, and contain all cluster monomials. The same family is an upper-cluster-algebra basis when the middle and upper algebras coincide. For a fixed Jacobian algebra and $\delta$-vector, the Newton polytope of the generic monodromy $F$-polynomial is independent of the order.

papers.title: Categorified Cluster Structures on Coulomb Branches of Certain Star-Shaped Quivers
papers.abstract: We study the quantized $K$-theoretic Coulomb branches of framed star-shaped quivers with central gauge dimension $n\geq2$, $r-1$ one-dimensional outer gauge vertices, and a one-dimensional framing at the central vertex. For $n=2$ and arbitrary $r\geq1$, and for every $n\geq2$ with $1\leq r\leq5$, we prove that the loop-graded Koszul-perverse heart is a monoidal categorification of the associated quantum cluster algebra over $\mathbb{Z}[v^{\pm1}]$. This quantum cluster algebra coincides with its upper quantum cluster algebra. For all $n\geq2$ and $r\geq1$, we construct an explicit initial seed and identify the associated upper quantum cluster algebra with the Grothendieck ring of this heart. Every mutation is realized by a short exact sequence, and every quantum cluster monomial is represented by a simple object.

papers.title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.

papers.title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology. This result enables the explicit computation of the hyperoctahedral homology of the universal enveloping algebras of involutive (DG) Lie algebras. For group algebras $k[\Gamma]$ equipped with the involution $g \mapsto g^{-1}$, we relate the involutive representation homology of $k[\Gamma]$ to the representation homology of the group $\Gamma$ with coefficients in $\mu_2$, and we show that the latter is the homology of the loop space of the mod $2$ Dold-Thom space of $B\Gamma$; more generally, we compute the representation homology of $\Gamma$ with coefficients in an arbitrary diagonalizable group scheme. As a consequence, the hyperoctahedral homology of $k[\Gamma]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ in characteristic $0$, for every $\Gamma$.

papers.title: Spectra and Support Theory for Wide Subcategories in $n$-Abelian Categories
papers.abstract: We develop a support theory for wide subcategories of essentially small Krull--Schmidt \(n\)-abelian categories. We construct spectra associated with families of wide subcategories and establish the corresponding support and radical theories. In particular, we characterize prime wide subcategories as the completely meet-irreducible elements of the lattice of wide subcategories and prove that every wide subcategory is recovered from the prime wide subcategories containing it. We further show that any classifying support datum is recovered, together with its object supports, from the canonical prime spectrum. Finally, we provide a \(2\)-abelian example admitting no classifying support datum.

papers.title: The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II
papers.abstract: We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $\varphi[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds. Our main result is a criterion, in terms of the faces of $P$, that determines when the Ehrhart ring of $P$ admits an invariant linear system of parameters of the correct representation type. We use these results to reduce the space of possible counterexamples to one of two cases. A randomised computer search produced counterexamples in each case. We also give an example where the equivariant $H^*$-series is effective but admits no invariant linear system of parameters, neither for $P$ nor any invariant subdivision of it, answering a question of Stapledon in the case of groups of order two.

papers.title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
papers.abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and F\'eray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.

papers.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $\mu\leq\lambda$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(\Phi,\mu,\lambda)$ the convex polytope $$P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda} = (\mu+C)\cap(\lambda-C)\cap(\overline{D}-\rho),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\Phi^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda}$ and $P^{\Phi'}_{\mu',\lambda'}$ are isometric, then $$K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)=K^{\Phi'}_{\lambda'\mu'}(q),$$ where $K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $\mu$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(\lambda)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

papers.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
papers.abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.

papers.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
papers.abstract: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $\tau$-locally free modules.

papers.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
papers.abstract: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).

papers.title: Stranding $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs
papers.abstract: Webs are planar directed graphs that encode invariant vectors for tensor products of fundamental $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-representations. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, web calculus is governed by effective reduction rules and well-understood reduced-web bases, but these features break down in higher rank. In this paper we develop a global combinatorial framework for untagged $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs, called \emph{strandings}, which organizes local labeling data into systems of colored directed paths on the web graph. Our main result is an explicit state-sum formula for the invariant vector of an untagged web as a weighted sum over its valid strandings. The usual labeling-based construction requires a choice of decomposition into elementary web pieces and a vertex-by-vertex coefficient calculation. Our global reformulation avoids both. We prove that the vectors produced by strandings are $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-invariant, compare the untagged theory with the tagged-web framework of Cautis, Kamnitzer, and Morrison, and use this comparison to obtain a complete set of relations for untagged web graphs. We also give applications of strandings to nonvanishing results, basis constructions from tableaux, and connections with Springer-theoretic combinatorics.

papers.title: Pointwise character bounds for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
papers.abstract: We present a basic pointwise bound for the irreducible characters of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and, as an application, derive new $L^p$ bounds for these characters. Our approach is based on the descent of characters to singular sets and the cancellation in this formula.

papers.title: Local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects
papers.abstract: We establish local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects in Hom-finite monoidal categories C over an algebraically closed field k. A separability morphism contracts the first two Hochschild cohomology groups without requiring an abelian ambient category. Separable algebra structures and homomorphisms from separable sources have open algebraic-group orbits, and affine Bezout estimates give effective finiteness results. For Frobenius subalgebras, exchange relations replace the source and embedding data by a single self-dual idempotent. We prove that their separable inner-conjugacy classes are open in the exchange locus, yielding a bound of 2^(dim_k(End_C(X))) for any ambient Frobenius algebra X; connectedness gives the same bound on the actual number of subalgebras. As an application, we obtain an effective form of the Etingof-Walton finiteness theorem: every finite-dimensional semisimple Hopf algebra H over C has fewer than 2^(dim_C(H)) left coideal subalgebras. In the unitary setting, we bound E-compatible intermediates of C*-algebra and von Neumann algebra inclusions up to unitary conjugacy, under finite-index and finite-center hypotheses. For irreducible finite-index subfactors N < M, we improve the 9^[M:N] bound of Bakshi-Das-Liu-Ren to fewer than 2^[M:N] intermediate subfactors.
